key_definitions.personal_information: Information relating to an identifiable living natural person or identifiable existing juristic person, including but not limited to name, ID number, contact details, biometrics, personal opinions, correspondence, financial/employment/criminal history
key_definitions.processing: Any operation concerning personal information including collection, receipt, recording, organisation, collation, storage, updating, modification, retrieval, alteration, consultation, use, dissemination, merging, linking, restriction, degradation, erasure or destruction
key_definitions.responsible_party: A public or private body or any other person which, alone or in conjunction with others, determines the purpose of and means for processing personal information
key_definitions.operator: A person who processes personal information for a responsible party in terms of a contract or mandate
key_definitions.data_subject: The person to whom personal information relates
key_definitions.consent: Any voluntary, specific and informed expression of will in terms of which permission is given for the processing of personal information
key_definitions.special_personal_information: Religious or philosophical beliefs, race or ethnic origin, trade union membership, political persuasion, health or sex life, biometric information, criminal behaviour
key_definitions.child: A natural person under the age of 18 years who is not legally competent

GDPR.relevance: POPIA was heavily influenced by GDPR. Many concepts are parallel.
key_differences: POPIA applies to juristic persons; GDPR does not
POPIA has criminal penalties up to 10 years imprisonment; GDPR relies on administrative fines
GDPR fines up to 4% of global turnover or EUR 20M; POPIA administrative fines up to R10M
POPIA has a single regulator; GDPR has one per member state
POPIA requires prior authorisation for certain processing; GDPR uses DPIA and prior consultation
GDPR has explicit right to data portability; POPIA does not
POPIA defines consent as voluntary, specific and informed; GDPR adds freely given and unambiguous

FICA.relevance: FICA mandates retention of financial records which may conflict with POPIA retention limits.
key_interactions: FICA requires 5-year retention of customer identification and transaction records
POPIA s14 retention must yield to FICA retention obligations
KYC/CDD data collection under FICA provides lawful basis under POPIA s11 (legal obligation)
Account number protections in POPIA s105-s106 complement FICA anti-fraud provisions

NCA.relevance: NCA governs credit information which is personal information under POPIA.
key_interactions: Credit bureau processing requires prior authorisation under POPIA s57
NCA prescribes retention periods for credit information that override POPIA s14
Consumers right to access credit records aligns with POPIA s23
Credit scoring is automated decision making under POPIA s71

ECT_Act.full_name: Electronic Communications and Transactions Act 25 of 2002
ECT_Act.relevance: ECT Act section 45 regulates unsolicited communications alongside POPIA s69.
key_interactions: ECT Act s45 prohibits spam; POPIA s69 adds consent requirements for direct marketing
ECT Act defines electronic communications referenced in POPIA
Both acts apply to transborder data flows
ECT Act cybercrime provisions complement POPIA breach notification

PAIA.full_name: Promotion of Access to Information Act 2 of 2000
PAIA.relevance: PAIA governs access to information and shares the Information Regulator with POPIA.
key_interactions: PAIA s51 manual must be updated to include POPIA processing information
POPIA s23 access requests follow PAIA procedures (s18 and s53)
The Information Regulator administers both PAIA and POPIA
PAIA grounds for refusal may limit POPIA access rights

Constitution.full_name: Constitution of the Republic of South Africa, 1996
Constitution.relevance: Section 14 of the Constitution enshrines the right to privacy which POPIA gives effect to.
key_interactions: POPIA s2 explicitly references the constitutional right to privacy
Constitutional right to freedom of expression (s16) balanced against privacy in POPIA s7
Right to administrative justice (s33) underpins enforcement provisions
Right to access information (s32) implemented through PAIA and intersects with POPIA

nli_pair_strategies: entailment: section X requires Y, premise restates requirement -> entailment
contradiction: section X prohibits Z, premise claims Z is allowed -> contradiction
neutral: section X addresses topic A, premise discusses related but distinct topic B -> neutral
exception_entailment: section X prohibits Y except when Z, premise states Z applies -> entails processing is allowed
multi_hop: section X references section Y which defines term Z -> chain reasoning
